original_test_intent: Verify that the selected GB-NV-PVP PCIe link can repeatedly transition from Gen1 to Gen2 five hundred times, settling at the required width and Gen2 speed each time without introducing link, endpoint, or platform errors.
original_method: Map the precise PCIe hierarchy and choose the approved Speed Change 12 operation; record baseline gen/width and errors; for each numbered iteration request the defined Gen1 state then Gen2 transition, observe LTSSM and settling, record negotiated gen/width and error deltas, and authorize the next transition only after acceptance; stop and recover at the first anomaly.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE approves the Speed Change 12 implementation and path; an operator isolates the SUT, monitors GPU/link/thermal health, and owns recovery if the transition loses the endpoint.
required_inputs: Mapped root port, switch/retimer, endpoint/GPU, and lane width
How Gen1 is established and Gen2 is requested
Expected width, LTSSM sequence, settle timeout, and transient allowance
Permitted AER/error deltas, 500-count semantics, aborts, and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated approved SUT and stable power/cooling
Verify target link before enabling transitions
Stop on failed/late Gen2, width downgrade, endpoint loss, new AER, GPU/host reset, thermal/power anomaly, or artifact gap
No automatic replay after a failed transition
agent_execution_scope: Validate package, topology, baseline, and approved limits
Run the pinned transition operation after authorization
Detect gaps or first failure and inhibit continuation
Do not choose the path or settle rule, alter unrelated links, retry, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Define Speed Change 12 and path-specific acceptance
Provide console recovery for link/GPU loss
Review every transition and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record the initial, requested, LTSSM-transitional, and settled link state with error deltas as one atomic result per iteration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the transition transaction, topology, deadlines, evidence, and recovery missing from the short source.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final Gen2 LnkSta proves only the last observation and cannot establish that every transition reached Gen2 at full width or avoided transient errors.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated link-speed control can downtrain, remove the GPU, reset devices, or affect sibling traffic depending on bridge/retimer topology.

review_improvement: Retains all 500 Gen1-to-Gen2 transitions while replacing a final-state shortcut with atomic path-specific evidence and safe first-fault control.
independent_technical_reasoning: A speed-change qualification result has two distinct dimensions: reaching the requested generation and retaining the required lane width without error. A link may negotiate Gen2 at reduced width, briefly enter recovery, or produce corrected errors and still look nominal in a later snapshot. The requested and settled states therefore need to be captured inside each iteration, with an explicit settle deadline and error-counter delta. The control must stop before iteration N+1 when N is ambiguous, otherwise repeated transitions can overwrite causality and amplify a marginal link failure.
